messages.subject: Creating a concordance data frame by filtering out the observations and meta information from an HTML-coded COHA concordance file
messages.subject_clean: Creating a concordance data frame by filtering out the observations and meta information from an HTML-coded COHA concordance file
messages.body_plain: Hello everyone, I'm trying to retrieve data from an HTML-coded file in order to put it together in a concordance data frame. To understand how I ended up with such files, I enumerate the steps: - 1) in the COHA web interface, I typed a construction in the query bar and selected the "KWIC" display so that each observation with its meta information appeared as a row in a concordance table; - 2) I right clicked on the concordance table and selected the option "Display frame source code". A new window opened with all the HTML code; - 3) I selected all the HTML code (Ctrl + A), copied it (Ctrl + C) and pasted it (Ctrl + V) into a text file; - 4) I repeated steps 2) and 3) for each page of the search results; As a next step, I had to identify the lines with the information on the concordance and the meta information. They are to be found in the following lines of code: # the identifier specifying the observation number (here, 958) 958 1888 # the year FIC # the text type DavidPoindexters A B C thrown at him, or, at any rate, not to understand them. Instead of going to the Lambert mansion, he had alighted at the inn, and Each observation was coded as such and as you can see, the context of the observation is repeated once. The idea would be to retrieve the concordance lines and the meta information in order to create a new concordance table. As a beginner, I would first create vectors for each concordance line, text ID, date and text type (after some clean-up session) and then paste them into a data frame. However, I would like to know whether one of you has better suggestions. I thank you very much for your help. Chris.

messages.body_plain: I finally found a better way to create a data frame with observations, contexts, dates and genres, using the following code. Saving the first tab-delimited table to a temp file is finally useless. For other people interested in using the HTML code of the KWIC results of a query in COHA, you can re-use it. The only requirement is to change the arguments in "all.matches.iso.3". #### This is a script to create a concordance table based on an HTML-coded concordance from COHA #### ### Create a table with just the observations with their preceding and subsequent contexts ### ## 1) Retrieve the lines in which the matches and their context occur rm(list=ls(all=T)) corpus.files<-choose.files() # import all the files with the concordance all.matches.iso<-vector() # create a vector to store the matches for(i in corpus.files) { # create a for-loop to extract the lines with the matches cat(i, "\n") current.corpus.file<-scan(i, what="char", sep="\n", quiet=T) current.sentences<-grep("", current.corpus.file, perl=T, value=T) all.matches.iso<-append(all.matches.iso, current.sentences) } ## 2) Isolate the line numbers from the tags all.matches.iso.2<-gsub("", "\\1\t", all.matches.iso, perl=T) ## 3) Replace the matches by matches with surrounding tab stops and delete remaining tags all.matches.iso.3<-gsub("(instead) (of) (.+ing?)", "\t\\1 \\2 \t\\3", all.matches.iso.2, perl=T, ignore.case=T) all.matches.iso.4<-gsub("", "", all.matches.iso.3, perl=T) ### Retrieve the dates of the matches ### ## 1) Retrieve the lines with the dates all.dates<-vector() # create a vector to store the dates for(i in corpus.files) { # create a for-loop to extract the lines with the matches cat(i, "\n") current.corpus.file<-scan(i, what="char", sep="\n", quiet=T) current.dates<-grep("\\d\\d\\d\\d", current.corpus.file, perl=T, value=T) all.dates<-append(all.dates, current.dates) } ## 2) Isolate the dates from the rest all.dates.2<-gsub("(\\d\\d\\d\\d)", "\\1", all.dates, perl=T) ### Retrieve the information about the text genres ### ## 1) Retrieve the lines with the meta information about text genres all.genres<-vector() # create a vector to store all the text genres per observations for(i in corpus.files) { # use a for-loop to extract the lines with the genres cat(i, "\n") current.corpus.file<-scan(i, what="char", sep="\n", quiet=T) current.genres<-grep("\\D+", current.corpus.file, perl=T, value=T) all.genres<-append(all.genres, current.genres) } ## 2) Isolate the text genres from the rest all.genres.2<-gsub("(\\w+)", "\\1", all.genres, perl=T) ### Create a data frame on the basis of the tab-delimited concordance table and the meta data ## 1) Split the tab-delimited table at every tab delimitation split.matches<-strsplit(all.matches.iso.4, "\t") ## 2) Prepare vectors to store the subsets of the resulting list index<-vector(); preceding.context<-vector(); match<-vector(); subsequent.context<-vector() ## 3) Extract the indices, the preceding contexts, the matches and the subsequent contexts into the vectors for(i in 1:length(split.matches)) { index[i]<-split.matches[[i]][1] preceding.context[i]<-split.matches[[i]][2] match[i]<-split.matches[[i]][3] subsequent.context[i]<-split.matches[[i]][4] } ## 4) Create a data frame with the vectors as columns new.data<-data.frame(index, preceding.context, match, subsequent.context, all.dates.2, all.genres.2) Le mercredi 23 mars 2016 01:47:17 UTC+1, Alex Perrone a écrit : > So you have a vector which contains everything you want, and fields are separated by the tab character?
